chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both)
about a woman who committed adultery, is she suitable to be taken as a wet nurse? He said: She is not suitable, nor is the milk of her daughter who was born from the adultery.

key_terms.تُسْتَرْضَعَ: to be taken as a wet nurse

ai.seo_question: Is a woman who committed adultery suitable to be a wet nurse in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*, Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (as) establishes that a woman who committed adultery is ineligible to be a wet nurse, extending the impurity to the milk of her daughter born specifically from that illicit union. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of linking physical purity and social suitability to the specific lineage and context of birth, distinguishing between general lineage and the immediate consequences of the act. It serves as a key precedent in the chapter of *Rada'ah* (breastfeeding) for determining the validity of milk transfer in cases of non-marital conception.
